title: Euler defect of contracting a nodal subcurve to a smooth point
statement:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Let $C,D$ be proper reduced $k$-schemes [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-pc-reduced-scheme] of pure dimension one [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension], and let $f:D\to C$ be a proper morphism. Let $y\in C(k)$ be a smooth point [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Suppose $B=(f^{-1}(y))_{\mathrm{red}}$ is a nonempty connected curve (pure of dimension one), with its reduced closed subscheme structure [def-weil-connected-scheme], and that $f:D\setminus B\to C\setminus\{y\}$ is an isomorphism. Assume $D$ is nodal on an open neighbourhood of $B$: at every nonsmooth point there its completed local ring is $k[[u,v]]/(uv)$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion, def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. Let $B_1,\ldots,B_v$ be the irreducible components of $B$ [def-weil-irreducible-components], let $e$ count its internal nodes (a self-node is counted once), and let $r$ count the distinct points of $B\cap\overline{D\setminus B}$, where the closure is taken in $D$. The normalizations $\widetilde B_i\to B_i$ [def-sc-normalization] are smooth proper connected curves. Put $g_i=\dim_k H^1(\widetilde B_i,\mathcal O_{\widetilde B_i})$ [def-sc-genus], and write $\chi(E)=\sum_j(-1)^j\dim_k H^j(E,\mathcal O_E)$ for the Euler characteristic of a proper $k$-scheme [def-pc-euler-characteristic]. Then
$$\chi(D)-\chi(C)=v-e-r-\sum_{i=1}^{v}g_i.$$
No equality of the two Euler characteristics, vanishing of any $g_i$, or tree property is assumed or asserted.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], $C,D$ are Noetherian: proper over $k$ implies finite type. Let $A=\overline{D\setminus B}_{\mathrm{red}}$ and $T=A\cap B$ be the scheme-theoretic intersection. Since $D$ is reduced and pure one-dimensional and $B$ is reduced, closed and pure one-dimensional, $B$ is a union of whole irreducible components and $A$ is the union of the other components. Indeed a proper closed subset of an irreducible Noetherian curve has dimension zero. Their radical ideals have intersection zero, so $D=A\cup B$ scheme-theoretically. Apply [lem-trf-nodal-subcurve-boundary], with $X=D$ and $Y=B$, using exactly the nodal neighbourhood assumed in the item. It gives nodality of $B$ and $T=\coprod_{j=1}^{r}\operatorname{Spec}k$, including the possibility $r=0$.

source.place: Tag 0E38 (lemma-closed-subscheme-nodal-curve), applied on the nodal neighbourhood; finite-type Noetherianity is morphisms.tex Tag 01T6.

proof.text: Let $h=f|_A:A\to C$. It is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence](a),(c), since $A\hookrightarrow D$ is closed. Away from $y$ it is the given isomorphism. Its fibre over $y$ has underlying set $A\cap B=|T|$, which is finite by Step 1; no assertion that the full fibre of $f$ is reduced is used. Thus every fibre of $h$ is finite. The target $C$ is locally Noetherian by Step 1, so [thm-pqf-finite-iff-proper-finite-fibres] makes $h$ finite. The same permanence node makes the closed subcurves $A,B,T$ proper over $k$.

source.place: Tag 02OG (lemma-characterize-finite); morphisms.tex Tags 01W3 and 01W5 for properness.

proof.text: Choose a smooth open neighbourhood $U$ of $y$ in $C$. By [lem-sc-smooth-normal], it is normal. Its finitely many irreducible components are disjoint: if two met, their distinct minimal primes would survive in a local ring, contradicting that a normal local ring is a domain. Retain the component containing $y$, so $U$ is integral. The reduced scheme $h^{-1}(U)$ is also integral: every component of $A$ contains its generic point in $D\setminus B$, since all components contained in the fibre were removed in forming $A$. Thus each component meeting $h^{-1}(U)$ meets $h^{-1}(U\setminus\{y\})$. The latter is isomorphic to the integral dense open $U\setminus\{y\}$, and consequently has exactly one generic point; hence $h^{-1}(U)$ has one irreducible component. Its reducedness now gives integrality. The finite map $h^{-1}(U)\to U$ induces an isomorphism of function fields through that dense-open isomorphism. Apply [lem-trf-finite-birational-normal-iso]. It is an isomorphism over $U$; together with the given isomorphism over $C\setminus\{y\}$ this proves that $h:A\xrightarrow{\sim}C$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 0AB1 (lemma-finite-birational-over-normal); smooth-normal input as in curves.tex (smooth curves over a field).

proof.text: Write $i_A,i_B,i_T$ for the three closed inclusions into $D$. Their restriction maps give the short exact sequence $$0\to\mathcal O_D\to i_{A,*}\mathcal O_A\oplus i_{B,*}\mathcal O_B\to i_{T,*}\mathcal O_T\to0,$$ where the last map is restriction from $A$ minus restriction from $B$. To check it on an affine chart with component-union ideals $I,J$, use $I\cap J=0$ from Step 1 and the exact ring-module sequence $$0\to R\to R/I\oplus R/J\to R/(I+J)\to0.$$ The kernel of the difference map consists precisely of pairs with equal image modulo $I+J$, which lift to one element of $R$; its surjectivity follows by lifting an element to the first summand. This proves exactness without an auxiliary contraction-cohomology assertion.

All four structure sheaves and their indicated direct images are coherent on these Noetherian schemes. By [lem-pc-closed-immersion-coherent-cohomology], closed direct image preserves coherence and all cohomology groups. Apply [lem-pc-euler-additive] to the exact sequence of Step 4, and to the split direct-sum sequence for its middle term. It gives $$\chi(D)=\chi(A)+\chi(B)-\chi(T).$$ Since $T$ is the finite disjoint union of $r$ copies of $\operatorname{Spec}k$, its global sections have dimension $r$ and no higher cohomology: global sections of modules on this finite discrete scheme is a finite product of module evaluation functors, which is exact. Hence $\chi(T)=r$. The isomorphism of Step 3 gives $\chi(A)=\chi(C)$, and therefore $$\chi(D)-\chi(C)=\chi(B)-r.$$ This remains valid if $D$ or $C$ is disconnected and if $r=0$.

source.place: Tag 08AA (lemma-euler-characteristic-additive); coherent.tex closed-immersion cohomology, or affine cohomology Tag 089W.

proof.text: The curve $B$ is proper by Step 2, reduced, connected and pure one-dimensional by the item, and nodal by Step 1. Its component normalizations are smooth proper connected curves by the item. Thus [lem-trf-nodal-curve-normalization-euler] applies with exactly the internal nodes and genera named in the statement and yields $$\chi(B)=v-e-\sum_{i=1}^{v}g_i.$$ Internal self-nodes contribute once; the $r$ boundary nodes are smooth as points of $B$ and have already been counted in Step 5.

proof.text: Substitute Step 6 into Step 5: $$\chi(D)-\chi(C)=(v-e-\sum_i g_i)-r=v-e-r-\sum_i g_i.$$ No equality of the two Euler characteristics, genus-zero condition or tree property enters this argument.
